'''''Ilex coriacea''''', sometimes known as '''large gallberry'''<ref name=PLANTS/> or '''sweet gallberry''',<ref name=iucnredlist/> is a shrub in the [[Aquifoliaceae|holly family]] native to coastal areas in the United States from [[Virginia]] to [[Texas]]. It exists primarily as an [[understory]] plant in [[pine]] forests, and is sometimes managed by [[controlled burn]]ings, resprouting from [[rhizome]]s.<ref name=feis1991>{{FEIS|type=shrub|last=Coladonato|first=Milo|year=1991|genus=Ilex|species=coriacea|access-date=25 April 2025}}</ref>

''Ilex coriacea'' is a [[facultative wetland]] plant<ref name=PLANTS/> and can be found in sandy, moist to wet soils<ref name=feis1991/> in [[bog]]s, at the edges of ponds<ref name=iucnredlist/> and in seepage swamps called [[baygall]]s.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=MacRoberts|first1=Barbara R.|last2=MacRoberts|first2=Michael H.|title=Floristics of Baygalls in Central Louisiana|journal=Phytologia|volume=86|issue=1|date=February 2004|url=http://biodiversitylibrary.org/part/220263|access-date=25 April 2025|via=Biodiversity Heritage Library}}</ref><ref>{{cite report|chapter-url=https://ecos.fws.gov/docs/recovery_plan/sfl_msrp/SFL_MSRP_Ecol%20Comm.pdf|chapter=The Ecological Communities|title=South Florida Multi-Species Recovery Plan|author=U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service|year=1999|location=Atlanta, Georgia|pages=500-502|access-date=25 April 2025}}</ref>  It is planted as an ornamental<ref name=iucnredlist/> and prefers acidic soils.<ref name=feis1991/>

The plant is an important [[nectar source]] for [[beekeeping|beekeepers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/ilex-coriacea/|title=''Ilex coriacea''|website=North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox|publisher=N.C. Cooperative Extension|access-date=25 April 2025}}</ref>
